# NVDA Quantitative Fundamental Report — Decision Date 2026-05-08

## 1. Revenue, Earnings & Margin Trajectory

NVDA's three available quarters show accelerating top-line growth and expanding profitability. Revenue rose from Q1 $44.06B to Q2 $46.74B to Q3 $57.01B, with QoQ growth of +22.0% in Q3 — the steepest sequential step-up in the window. Earnings followed: EPS advanced from $0.76 → $1.08 → $1.30 (+20.4% QoQ in Q3); net income climbed from $18.77B → $26.42B → $31.91B.

**Margin expansion is the standout feature.** Gross margin widened from 60.5% (Q1) to 72.4% (Q2) to 73.4% (Q3), indicating extreme operating leverage as revenue scales against a largely fixed cost base. Operating margin moved from 49.1% → 60.8% → 63.2% in tandem. Net margin reached 55.9% in Q3. The ratio panel confirms durable profitability: gross_margin=69.8%, operating_margin=58.1%, net_margin=52.4% on a trailing basis as of 2026-05-07. ROE is an exceptional 0.865, supported by the profit machine rather than financial leverage.

**Cash generation tracks earnings.** Operating cash flow was $27.41B (Q1), $15.37B (Q2), $23.75B (Q3). The Q3 figure shows a QoQ recovery of +54.6%. Free cash flow is unavailable, but operating cash flow across three quarters totals $66.53B — roughly 68% of cumulative net income ($77.10B), indicating real cash conversion rather than accrual-driven earnings. No systematic cash-flow-to-earnings divergence is visible.

## 2. Balance-Sheet Resilience

The balance sheet is fortress-grade. Total debt has been essentially flat at ~$8.47B across all three quarters while total equity expanded from $83.84B → $100.13B → $118.90B — a $35B increase in seven months driven entirely by retained earnings. The debt-to-equity ratio stands at 0.085 (8.5% of equity). Total liabilities ($42.25B) represent only 26.2% of total assets ($161.15B). There is no meaningful balance-sheet risk; the company is self-funding its growth entirely from operations.

## 3. Valuation vs. Own History

Valuation is stretched. On 2026-05-07: pe_diluted=59.9x sits near the top of the 365-day range (43.2–63.5); p_b=51.8x at 39.6–57.9; p_s=31.4x. The earnings yield of 1.7% is well below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.41% — a negative spread of ~270 bps. Over the trailing twelve observation points, PE has oscillated between ~46x (2025-06-11) and ~60x (current), with a central tendency around 51–55x. The current reading marks the upper bound of the historical window. Price-to-earnings expansion from ~50x in early April to ~60x by early May represents a ~20% multiple re-rating in one month absent a new earnings print — this is multiple momentum, not a fundamental re-pricing.

At a 1.7% earnings yield, the market is pricing either sustained multi-year double-digit earnings growth or perpetual premium multiples. Neither is quantifiable from the three-quarter panel alone, and the absence of YoY or TTM data prevents a growth-adjusted valuation (e.g., PEG). The valuation embeds a high bar.

## 4. Price Context vs. Fundamentals

Close on 2026-05-07 was $211.50, near the 365-day high of $216.82 and up +23.1% over the prior quarter (from $171.88 on 2026-02-05). The stock has recovered from a Q4-to-Q1 drawdown that saw it dip to the 365-day low of $115.21. Price action has broadly tracked the earnings improvement — the Q3 earnings beat coincided with a rally. However, the magnitude of the recent advance (+23% in ~63 trading days) has outpaced the QoQ earnings growth (+20%), indicating some multiple expansion layered on top of fundamental improvement. The price is near all-time highs; there is limited margin-of-safety from a chart perspective.

## 5. Macro & Sentiment Overlays

**Macro context is mixed-to-challenging for the valuation framework.** 10-year yields at 4.41% (up from ~4.22% over the quarter) and the 2-year at 3.92% (up from ~3.48%) reflect a steepening short-end and broadly higher rate environment. The 10Y-2Y spread has compressed to 0.49% from 0.74% three months prior. WTI crude oil has surged to $98.38/bbl (+52.4% over the lookback), potentially pressuring enterprise capex budgets and input costs broadly. Corporate credit spreads (Baa at 6.06%) are elevated. VIX has normalized to 17.08 after spiking above 31 in late March. Fed funds at 3.63% suggest modest easing has occurred but remains restrictive relative to NVDA's earnings yield.

**News sentiment is neutral.** The 90-day mean score of 0.454 indicates mildly positive but unremarkable sentiment. No sustained bullish or bearish trend is evident in the daily series; recent readings cluster around 0.3–0.55.

## 6. Strongest Quantitative Upside & Downside

**Upside:** Gross margin expansion from 60.5% to 73.4% in two quarters suggests a structural step-change in business mix or pricing power. If sustained at ~73% gross margins, even modest revenue growth compounds earnings at an extraordinary rate. The balance sheet (debt-to-equity=0.085) provides ample capacity for capital return or investment. The three-quarter revenue CAGR of +13.6% per quarter annualizes to ~66%.

**Downside:** The PE of 59.9x at the top of its range requires flawless execution. Earnings yield (1.7%) is 270 bps below the risk-free rate; any re-rating toward the midpoint of the historical PE range (~52x) implies ~13% downside. The absence of YoY comparables means growth durability is assumed, not demonstrated. The sharp Q1-to-Q2 cost-of-revenue drop ($17.39B → $12.89B) against rising revenue is unexplained and warrants scrutiny — if Q1 contained a one-time item inflating costs, the margin trajectory may be flatter than the trajectory suggests.

## Provisional Conclusion

The business fundamentals are extraordinarily strong: accelerating revenue, expanding margins, robust cash generation, and a clean balance sheet. These are not in question. However, the stock is trading at the top of its historical valuation range (PE=59.9x vs. 365-day range 43.2–63.5) with a negative spread to risk-free rates. Price has already re-rated sharply. The quantitative picture is one of a superb business at an ambitious price — **fundamental attractiveness is high, but entry-level attractiveness is diminished by valuation that has already captured much of the improvement.** The PM's judgment on growth durability beyond the visible three-quarter window will determine whether 60x is justified or whether a pullback toward the ~50x midpoint represents the better opportunity.

# NVDA — Qualitative Franchise & Narrative Assessment

**Decision date:** 2026-05-08 | **Report date:** 2026-05-08

---

## 1. Business / Franchise Read

NVIDIA is the dominant platform provider for AI infrastructure. The structural web_search evidence paints a clear picture: the company controls approximately 80–92% of the high-end data center GPU market (estimates vary by source and measurement), with its closest merchant competitor AMD at 5–7%. Data Center revenue represented ~88–90% of total sales in FY2026 (ended Jan 2026), up from 78% two years prior, making NVIDIA effectively a pure-play AI infrastructure business. Total FY2026 revenue reached $215.9B (+65% YoY), with data center alone at $193.7B.

The franchise moat rests on three pillars: (1) CUDA software ecosystem with 5M+ registered developers creating deep switching costs; (2) full-stack integration spanning GPUs, networking (InfiniBand/Spectrum-X), and pre-configured systems (DGX); and (3) fabless capital efficiency — outsourcing manufacturing to TSMC while retaining priority access to advanced nodes, enabling ROIC well above 200% and gross margins near 73–75%. The business model generates revenue through high-ticket hardware, recurring SaaS via NVIDIA AI Enterprise (~$4,500/GPU/year), gaming GPUs (>$10B annually), and emerging automotive/robotics platforms.

Capital allocation is tilted toward buybacks over dividends ($50B authorization announced mid-2024), with a modest quarterly cash dividend. More recently, NVIDIA has adopted an "AI foundation portfolio" strategy — taking significant equity stakes in ecosystem partners and AI labs (reported ~$30B in OpenAI, ~$10B in Anthropic, $2B in Nebius/Marvell, $500M in Corning warrants, $1B Nokia stake) to reinforce its GPU, networking, and AI factory franchises. This is a distinctive strategic lever that deepens ecosystem lock-in while capturing upstream AI value.

## 2. Recent Developments (Dated Events)

**Earnings catalyst (May 20):** NVIDIA reports Q1 FY2027 on May 20. Management guided $78B in revenue (+77% YoY), with Wall Street consensus at ~$78.8B and whisper numbers higher. Goldman Sachs raised estimates by ~12%, expecting Q1 revenue of $80.05B and a "beat-and-raise" quarter (2026-05-07, Benzinga). For Q2, consensus sits at ~$86.6B (+85% YoY). The company projects $1 trillion in cumulative orders through Blackwell and Vera Rubin by end of 2027 (multiple sources, Apr-May 2026).

**China — effectively zero official market share:** Multiple sources confirm NVIDIA has been "effectively foreclosed" from China's data center compute market. U.S. export restrictions and Chinese government actions have driven official market share to zero, though a booming gray market persists with B300 servers reportedly selling at ~$1M per unit in China — nearly double U.S. prices (2026-05-04, Benzinga). Senator Coons has demanded clarification on conflicting H200 export approval statements (2026-05-02, Benzinga). The Trump administration is planning official AI dialogue with China at a potential mid-May summit (2026-05-07, Benzinga).

**Hyperscaler capex acceleration:** Major cloud customers continue to expand AI budgets: Alphabet raised capex guidance to $180–190B with even higher 2027 plans; Meta raised its 2026 capex to $125–145B (nearly double 2025); Amazon committed $200B in 2026 capex. These signals are structurally positive for near-term NVIDIA demand.

**Strategic investments & partnerships:** NVIDIA invested $500M in Corning warrants for optical fiber infrastructure (2026-05-07), partnered with TotalEnergies on a €100M+ AI supercomputer (2026-05-06), and announced Ising — an open-source quantum AI model platform (2026-05-03). The Vera Rubin architecture, expected H2 2026, promises ~90% inference cost reduction versus Blackwell.

**Supply chain risk — helium shortage:** The Iran/Strait of Hormuz conflict has taken ~30% of global helium production offline (Qatar's Ras Laffan facility), with helium critical for EUV lithography and wafer cooling. Even if the conflict resolves, repairs could take years, creating potential production bottlenecks for NVIDIA's TSMC-manufactured chips (2026-04-28, multiple sources).

## 3. Material Risks & Offsets

**Custom silicon erosion (structural, multi-year):** The most credible long-term threat. Hyperscaler custom ASICs (Google TPU, AWS Trainium/Inferentia, Microsoft Maia) collectively represent a growing share of the accelerator market. Broadcom's AI ASIC revenue hit ~$20B+ in FY2025 with a $73B backlog. Amazon's custom chip business reached a $20B annual run rate. However, these are concentrated in inference workloads, and NVIDIA's CUDA/software moat remains intact for training at scale. Inference: *the transition from NVIDIA monopoly to a three-tier competitive structure (NVIDIA 60–75%, AMD 10–15%, custom 15–25%) is plausible by 2028, but TAM expansion from ~$200B to $500B+ means all three can grow simultaneously.*

**China regulatory & geopolitical risk (confirmed):** Export controls have permanently impaired NVIDIA's China access and are actively benefiting competitors building developer ecosystems. The regulatory environment remains fluid — the AI Diffusion IFR was rescinded but a replacement rule is pending; the GAIN AI Act adds further uncertainty. This is a confirmed, material headwind to total addressable market.

**Customer concentration (structural):** Four hyperscalers account for >50% of data center revenue. Any shift toward capital discipline or accelerated adoption of custom chips directly compresses NVIDIA's growth. Current evidence suggests the opposite — capex is accelerating — but this risk is real on a 2–3 year horizon.

**Helium/supply chain disruption (near-term, event-driven):** The Strait of Hormuz helium shortage is a concrete near-term production risk for TSMC-fabricated chips. Samsung and SK Hynix face the most direct exposure, with potential downstream impact on NVIDIA's Blackwell GPU shipments.

**Valuation normalization risk (market/inference):** At ~24x forward P/E (vs. 10-year avg ~62x), NVIDIA appears modestly valued relative to its own history, but the stock's $4.8T market cap embeds expectations of sustained hypergrowth. Any deceleration in hyperscaler spending or competitive pricing pressure could trigger multiple compression.

**Offsets:** Vera Rubin's 90% inference cost reduction could reassert NVIDIA's leadership in inference (the fastest-growing workload category). The $1T order backlog through 2027 provides near-term revenue visibility. The AI foundation portfolio strategy creates ecosystem optionality. Software monetization (AI Enterprise, NIM) is an underappreciated high-margin recurring revenue stream.

## 4. Qualitative Assessment

**Positive-leaning.** NVIDIA possesses one of the most durable franchise positions in the semiconductor industry: an unmatched software ecosystem (CUDA), structural capital efficiency (fabless, ~75% gross margins), and an expanding full-stack platform moat. The immediate demand picture is exceptionally strong — hyperscaler capex is accelerating, Q1 guidance implies 77% growth, and Goldman Sachs expects a beat-and-raise cycle. The forward P/E of ~24x appears reasonable for a business growing earnings at this rate.

The franchise quality is not in question; what is in question is the *duration and degree* of current pricing power. Custom silicon adoption by hyperscalers, China market loss, and eventual AI spending normalization are real structural headwinds that will compress margins and growth rates over a 3–5 year horizon. The China foreclosure is already confirmed and material. However, these risks are well-flagged and largely reflected in NVIDIA's significant multiple compression from historical levels.

Near-term catalysts (May 20 earnings, Vera Rubin launch, ongoing capex acceleration) are structurally supportive. The helium supply risk is a genuine near-term wildcard but is event-driven and resolvable. On balance, the franchise narrative supports fundamental attractiveness — NVIDIA is a high-quality business entering its earnings report from a position of strength, with risks that are structural rather than existential.
